pr_title: roachtest: test selector causes test starvation due to decommissioned tests
pr_body:
As a part of the test selection is explained in https://cockroachlabs.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/TE/pages/3596091522/Test+Selection+for+roachtest+nightlies, we currently sort all tests by the last run and create 2 groups as selected and unselected. Out of the unselected tests, we select 35% of tests.

But, if tests are decommissioned, the test selector does not know about that as test selector data is from snowflake and has no information of whether a test is decommissioned or temporarily removed. But, if decommissioned tests are considered, they can cause starvation for other tests as they always appear in the top of the list for selection as their last run date will never change as they never run and the tests are sorted by last run date.

To fix this, this PR creates an intersection of the tests that are selected by test selector and the tests are part of the run. From that 35% of the tests are selected.

Fixes: #128780
Epic: none
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/128785)
Thanks for the review @DarrylWong ! I have addressed your comments. Please do let me know if it is good.

> I'm approving, but I think that it'd be nice to have some unit tests for this. We should be able to verify that the test selector is working without having to run the entire roachtest suite. Doing that is costly and mostly manual validation.
> 
> Something along the lines of mocking the snowflake query to hit all the interesting edge cases? i.e. test hasn't run in 4 days, test is new, test is skipped, etc. Then we check that the selected tests are what we expect. Maybe a datadriven test would be applicable here?

Absolutely agree with the above. The lack of unit tests is concerning, especially for something that's on a critical path. At minimum, we should add sanity checks and post violations via the existing slack integration. This could be done as a follow-up PR to facilitate reviewing and backporting.

Thanks @srosenberg and @DarrylWong ! Sure, it totally makes sense to have UT to validate and guard against any unwanted changes. I will have a ticket open for the same. Regarding alerting, I am talking to the data team and will need to work on what can be done there.

Just to clarify, I actually run the test selection locally to ensure its correctness rather than executing the roachtest suite in teamcity.

> Just to clarify, I actually run the test selection locally to ensure its correctness rather than executing the roachtest suite in teamcity.

I think I've seen at least a couple of instances where we ran the roachtest suite on TC to test the selection logic (the most recent occurrence was talked about [in this internal thread](https://cockroachlabs.slack.com/archives/C023S0V4YEB/p1724173395007399)). It's fine to run a fraction of the suite on a branch from time to time, but even in those cases we should never be setting `TC_BUILD_BRANCH` to master.

issue_context.title: roachtest: test selector causes test starvation because of decommissioned tests
issue_context.body:
If there are tests that have been decommissioned, those causes test starvation for other successful tests for 7 days.

This is because the decommissioned tests are not run. So, the last run for these tests will never get updated and will remain in the top of the test selection list.

After 7 days, they are selected for run by the “test not run for the last 7 days” criteria and those tests move out of the “35% successful test selection” criteria.

Jira issue: CRDB-41203
